note: The same tetrapod at a scurry: shorter cycle, duty under a half so each set is in the air longer than it is down, a longer reach and a lower body. The stagger is halved -- at speed the ripple compresses -- and the abdomen bounces harder because at this cadence it is the mass that lags. The bind pose holds legs I, II and IV at full stretch, so `legHold` draws their stance stations in toward the body -- the front pair back, the back pair forward -- to give the stride somewhere to go; leg III stands sideways and its step is a swing at the hip, not a reach.
